resources.string: Turn on “Mask” and swipe over the cells you want to ignore (trees, curtains, clocks).
Audio changes apply to the next clip.
The camera runs in the background. You can turn the screen off, recording continues. Stop it here or with “Close” in the notification.
Point the camera, set the sensitivity and mask, then tap “Start camera” and turn the screen off.
If this phone works as a camera, set a PIN or screen lock password on it: otherwise anyone who picks up the phone gets access to the camera and the recordings.
This phone can\'t encode HEVC (H.265) in hardware, so recording will use H.264. Files will be a bit larger, but everything works. To make files smaller, lower the bitrate or resolution in Settings.
So the system doesn\'t kill the camera while the screen is off, allow the app to run without battery restrictions. A system window will appear now: tap “Allow”.
The camera is running: changes to recording (resolution, FPS, grid, rotation) apply after it restarts.
Uses the phone\'s own camera. Rotation is automatic (accelerometer).
A USB webcam connected through an OTG adapter, instead of the phone\'s own camera. Experimental: webcam support varies a lot between models.
The camera is running: the source changes after it restarts.

Connect the webcam via an OTG adapter before starting the camera. The first time, do it with the app open (preview screen) so Android can show the one-time permission prompt — it then remembers the choice for this webcam.
A target resolution — the webcam may deliver a different one depending on what it supports; the picture is scaled to fit.
Set manually: the webcam is mounted separately from the phone, so there is no accelerometer to detect this automatically.
Permission to access the USB camera was denied
No USB webcam found. Connect it via an OTG adapter.
The camera can\'t do %1$d fps at this resolution

≈ %1$d MB per hour of continuous recording. Resolution is picture sharpness, bitrate is how much data goes into each second of video: 720p at a good bitrate often looks better than 1080p at a poor one.
Rotation is detected automatically by the phone\'s accelerometer, no setting needed: the video is recorded the way the phone is mounted.
Cells along the long side of the frame
Cells along the short side of the frame
Default is 16×9. For a portrait frame the grid turns by itself (9×16). Changing the grid resets the mask. Sensitivity and mask are set on the main screen.
Minimum gap between beeps while motion continues
A short double beep plays through the speaker when motion is detected — like a chime, not part of the recording. Uses the alarm volume, so it stays audible even in silent mode.
The camera is off by schedule now.

Outside these hours the camera turns off completely: the phone doesn\'t heat up or drain, and passing cars at night aren\'t recorded. Drive upload, cleanup and timelapse keep working. The window can span midnight (for example 20:00 to 07:00). Switching happens within 30 seconds of the set time.
Built at the end of the day, at 23:55, from the clips of the whole day.

A sped-up video of the chosen length is built from the motion clips of the selected hours. If there was little motion the video is shorter, there are no filler frames. If there was no motion at all, no video is created.
No clips in the selected hours
Upload works over Wi-Fi and mobile data. Without a connection, files wait in a queue. Structure: “%1$s” → date → part of day; the timelapse sits in the date folder.
If sign-in shows an “app not found” error: in Google Cloud Console → Clients create an Android OAuth client with these values (details in the README). Tap a row to copy it.
Google didn\'t recognize this app (error 10). In Google Cloud Console create an Android OAuth client with the package name and SHA-1 from the settings below (see README) and try again.
How many days to keep source clips on Google Drive
How many days to keep source clips on the phone
Estimate at 2 hours of motion per day: Drive over %1$d d will take about %2$s GB (at the current recording bitrate). This is the heaviest part.
How many days to keep timelapses on Google Drive
How many days to keep timelapses on the phone
A timelapse is about two orders of magnitude smaller than the clips, so it usually makes sense to keep it much longer.
The free 15 GB of a Google account is shared with mail and photos. Recordings older than the set period are deleted automatically, checked every few hours.
